doc.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Tuba to string bass and bringing both to the job
summary: Bassists were asked to bring both tuba and bass; Haggart mentions Vince Giordano doing the same today.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: That’s what I was going to ask about, when they made the switch.
Was there a time when you were expected to play both?

Oh, yeah. They’d say, “Bring both.” You’d bring them both on the job. Imagine bringing a tuba and a string bass both. There’s a guy today that, Vince Giordano, who plays the bass sax, and he brings all three. Not only that, he sets up the music stands and microphones, a PA system, plus bringing his three instruments, the string bass, the bass saxophone and a tuba. And the poor guy is very discouraged. He’s in New York but he can’t get much work for his band, and I know he’s thinking of chucking the whole thing. But he’s playing music of the ‘20s and ‘30s, and these are all young guys. And it’s really a kick to hear those arrangements which he makes and he has a couple of other arrangers in the band. They are all New York musicians and they’re all young, and they’re all playing the music they played back then. They’re not playing any kind of rock & roll or anything like that, they’re not playing bebop, they’re just playing— and there’s this whole gang of good players that know all the old songs, and play jazz the way Ralph and I play it. You know, they play those same tunes.
